subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: 3D Printing: Manufacturing Without Factories
description: One-minute skill: 3D Printing: Manufacturing Without Factories.

hook.text: In 2023, a startup 3D-printed a house in Texas in 48 hours. It cost $10,000.

buildup.text: 3D printers build objects layer by layer from digital files. Plastics, metals, concrete — even human tissue.

discovery.text: Traditional manufacturing cuts away material. 3D printing adds only what's needed. Waste drops to near zero.

twist.text: NASA tested 3D-printed rocket engine parts. They performed better than traditionally machined ones.

climax.text: Doctors 3D-print custom implants matched to a patient's exact anatomy. No two are alike.

punchline.text: No factory. No mold. Just a file and a printer.

quiz.question: Why does 3D printing produce less waste than traditional manufacturing?
options: It uses biodegradable materials that decompose quickly
It adds only the material needed instead of cutting away excess
It recycles failed prints automatically inside the machine
